xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4929: Workspace creation runs npm install at a polyrepo root that has no package.json, so pan start fails for Mind Your Now

plan.title: Workspace creation runs npm install at a polyrepo root that has no package.json, so pan start fails for Mind Your Now
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: createWorkspace (src/lib/workspace-manager/create.ts) runs `<pm> install` at the workspace root unconditionally. A polyrepo workspace root has no package.json, so npm walks up to ~/Projects (which has node_modules), fails, writes a stray package-lock.json there, and since #4163 (2026-09-24) the failure aborts creation, so every MYN and botland pan start fails. MIN-1071..1076 hit the same failure and were rescued by a hand-written stub package.json.
narratives.Proposal: Skip the root install (step 'No root package.json; skipped root install') when the root has no package.json, via a small shared helper (dependency-install.ts). Add an opt-in RepoConfig.package_manager so a polyrepo repo can request a host-side install inside its own directory; unset means no install (MYN's container owns fe deps, matching verification-runner). Apply the same root guard to the legacy CLI install path. Document both.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Automatic per-repo installs based on lockfile or package.json presence without the opt-in field
- Per-repo installs on later `pan workspace add-repo` / addReposToWorkspace
- Lockfile-based package-manager auto-detection for the root install
- The PAN-4553 'dashboard is not responding' message (already gated on fetch failed by 96372988c0c)
- Deleting stray ~/Projects/package-lock.json or old MYN stub package.json files
- Converting CLI execSync calls in workspace-create.ts to async
- Changing the MYN projects.yaml entry
- Changing verification-runner.ts polyrepo behavior

autoDecisions.summary: Per-repo installs are opt-in through a new repos[].package_manager field instead of running automatically in every repo with a package.json.
autoDecisions.rationale: Host pnpm is broken on this machine (corepack cannot find pnpm 12.4.2), MYN's init-fe container owns fe/node_modules with a container-path pnpm store that a host install would conflict with, myn-skills would gain an untracked package-lock.json, and verification-runner.ts already treats polyrepo deps as container/gate-owned. The opt-in field still delivers the issue's 'respect a per-repo package manager' capability.

autoDecisions.summary: The legacy CLI install path in src/cli/commands/workspace-create.ts gets the same package.json guard.
autoDecisions.rationale: Same bug on a sibling path (non-fatal there, but it still writes a stray lockfile into an ancestor); a three-line change using the shared helper.

autoDecisions.summary: The fix PR closes duplicates PAN-4553 and PAN-4390.
autoDecisions.rationale: Both report the identical failure and cause; leaving them open would strand them after the fix lands.

autoDecisions.summary: The docs are corrected to match the code's bun.lock-else-npm detection rather than adding lockfile detection.
autoDecisions.rationale: Adding detection would change root-install behavior for monorepo projects outside this issue's scope.

items.title: Skip the root dependency install in createWorkspace when the workspace root has no package.json

expected_outputs: tests/lib/workspace-manager.test.ts passes including 'skips the root install when a polyrepo workspace root has no package.json', 'runs the root install when a monorepo workspace root has a package.json' and 'fails creation when the root install fails'

narrative.Action: Follow PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4929.md WI-1 exactly. Create src/lib/workspace-manager/dependency-install.ts exporting hasPackageJson(dir) and installCommandFor(pm). In src/lib/workspace-manager/create.ts, wrap the root install block (comment 'Install dependencies using the project's package manager.' up to 'Package installers such as Husky') in `if (!hasPackageJson(workspacePath)) { steps.push('No root package.json; skipped root install'); progress(..., 'complete') } else { <existing block unchanged, using installCommandFor> }`. Add the three named tests to describe('createWorkspace') in tests/lib/workspace-manager.test.ts using the existing mockExecAsync/isWorktreeAddCall/registerProject scaffolding. Use execAsync only (server-reachable). The commit message body must contain 'Closes #4553', 'Closes #4390' and the Root cause paragraph from the PRD.

items.title: Given a polyrepo project whose workspace root has no package.json, when createWorkspace runs, then it returns success: true, its steps contain exactly 'No root package.json; skipped root install', and no exec call ends in ' install'.

Given a monorepo project whose worktree has a package.json and package_manager npm, when createWorkspace runs, then it calls execAsync with 'npm install' and cwd equal to the workspace path and its steps contain 'Installed dependencies (npm)'.

Given a root install that rejects, when createWorkspace runs on a workspace root with a package.json, then it still returns success: false with an error starting 'Dependency install failed (' (existing behavior preserved).

Given the pushed root-install-guard commit, when `git log -1 --format=%B` is read, then the message contains 'Closes #4553', 'Closes #4390', and a root-cause paragraph naming ada4f64db4d (2026-04-14) and #4163 (2026-09-24) and stating MIN-1071..1076 were rescued by a hand-written stub package.json.
Run opt-in per-repo installs for polyrepo repos that set repos[].package_manager

expected_outputs: tests/lib/workspace-manager.test.ts passes including 'runs a per-repo install only for repos that set package_manager' and 'fails creation when a per-repo install fails'

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-2 exactly. Add `package_manager?: 'bun' | 'npm' | 'pnpm'` with the PRD's doc comment to RepoConfig in src/lib/workspace-config.ts. In create.ts, directly after the root-install block, loop workspaceConfig.repos (polyrepo only): skip symlink repos and repos without package_manager; skip silently if the repo dir is missing; push '<name>: no package.json; skipped install' when the dir has no package.json; otherwise execAsync(installCommandFor(pm), { cwd: repoDir }) and push 'Installed dependencies in <name> (<pm>)'; on failure push 'Dependency install failed in <name> (<pm>): <msg first 200>', set success=false, progress error, return. Add the two named tests.

items.title: Given polyrepo repos fe (package_manager pnpm, has package.json), api (no field, has package.json) and docs (symlink, package_manager npm), when createWorkspace runs, then exactly one install call occurs: 'pnpm install' with cwd <workspace>/fe, and steps contain 'Installed dependencies in fe (pnpm)'.

Given repo fe with package_manager pnpm whose install rejects with 'pnpm boom', when createWorkspace runs, then it returns success: false and errors contain a string starting 'Dependency install failed in fe (pnpm): pnpm boom'.

Given a repo with package_manager set whose directory has no package.json, when createWorkspace runs, then it produces the step '<name>: no package.json; skipped install' and runs no install in that repo.
Guard the legacy pan workspace create install path on package.json

expected_outputs: git grep prints exactly one match in src/cli/commands/workspace-create.ts
metadata.acJustification: Two ACs: the change is a single guard on a CLI-only path with no existing test harness; the helper it calls is tested by root-install-guard.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-4. docs/WORKSPACE-DEPENDENCIES.md: replace the false lockfile auto-detect sentence (line ~65) with 'If omitted, Overdeck uses bun when the workspace root has a bun.lock, and npm otherwise.'; add the no-package.json skip sentence quoting 'No root package.json; skipped root install'; reword Workspace Creation Flow step 2 (line ~160). configuration/polyrepo.mdx: add a commented `# package_manager: pnpm` line to the fe repo example and a '## Dependency installs in polyrepo workspaces' section before '## Template Placeholders' with the content listed in the PRD (root skip, opt-in field with values bun/npm/pnpm, leave unset when a devcontainer installs deps because a host install can conflict with the container's pnpm store, failure is fatal and a re-run resumes).
